text: Risk management is the process of identifying possible problems before they happen. First, you need to find the risks that could affect your project, such as budget cuts or delays. After that, you create mitigation strategies to reduce the chance or impact of these risks. For example, you might train staff or buy insurance. It is also wise to prepare contingency plans, which are backup actions if things go wrong. Finally, you must keep monitoring the risks, because new ones can appear at any time. By following these steps, you can protect your goals and make better decisions.
